system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

It shall be possible for the user to review the message at a later time. 4. The delivery of the emergency alert shall not preempt an active voice or data session. 5. The mobile device shall be capable to perform duplicate detection. 6. Mobile devices shall support receiving and displaying emergency alerts in Arabic and English. 7. Handsets shall only be required to receive and present emergency alerts in languages as issued by the Alert Originator. 8. It shall be possible for the emergency alerts to be displayed on the handset upon reception and without any user interaction. 9. The handset shall not support any capabilities to reply, forward or copy the received emergency alerts. 10. data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 3 pages (GSM-7) and Arabic is 6 pages (UCS-2), both well under the 15-page maximum. Encodings fit each script. The first page of each language opens with the hazard (fog warning / تحذير من الضباب) and the area and times. Length beyond one page is the recorded gap G6 and is not objected to again.

no_basis.concern: The TDRA-TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, while both language versions run to several pages. This conflicts with the handset spec, which sets no page limit, and with the 15-page maximum. It is already covered by recorded gap G6.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE page limit for cell broadcast messages above 1 page

no_basis.concern: The first page may not carry an explicit protective action. The text states the hazard, area and times, but no instruction such as driving carefully. The action cannot be judged beyond the text shown, and this is a content matter for the content reviewers.
no_basis.searched_for: cell broadcast first page must carry hazard and action
